Goal: comment author edits own comment via PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id, body {"comment":{"body":"..."}}. Route: article.controller.ts. Logic: article.service.ts.

Rules (values are read from source, not copied here):
1. Author-only edit. Source: article.service.ts, deleteComment and updateArticle. No edit rule found; assumed same.
2. Auth required. Source: article.controller.ts, main.ts.
3. Edit time limit. NOT FOUND in repo. Do not enforce one.
4. Edited mark. NOT FOUND as explicit rule. Source: schema.prisma, Comment.updatedAt. Assumed: edit sets updatedAt, as updateArticle does. No migration then. A separate flag's migration rule: NOT FOUND.
5. Error shape and status codes. Sources conflict: main.ts (error message as body) vs article.service.ts throws. Followed: deleteComment, the sibling action.
6. Migrations. Source: README.md, package.json, src/prisma/migrations/. Never hand-edit migration_lock.toml.
7. Unit tests. Source: jest.config.ts, project.json, src/tests/. Run: npm test.

Acceptance: author edit succeeds; others refused; unit tests cover both.

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

generator client {
  provider        = "prisma-client-js"
  previewFeatures = []
}

model Article {
  id          Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  slug        String    @unique
  title       String
  description String
  body        String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime  @default(now())
  tagList     Tag[]
  author      User      @relation("UserArticles", fields: [authorId], onDelete: Cascade, references: [id])
  authorId    Int
  favoritedBy User[]    @relation("UserFavorites")
  comments    Comment[]
}

model Comment {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @default(now())
  body      String
  article   Article  @relation(fields: [articleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  articleId Int
  author    User     @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  Int
}

model Tag {
  id       Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  name     String    @unique
  articles Article[]
}

model User {
  id         Int       @id @default(autoincrement())
  email      String    @unique
  username   String    @unique
  password   String
  image      String?   @default("https://api.realworld.io/images/smiley-cyrus.jpeg")
  bio        String?
  articles   Article[] @relation("UserArticles")
  favorites  Article[] @relation("UserFavorites")
  followedBy User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  following  User[]    @relation("UserFollows")
  comments   Comment[]
  demo       Boolean   @default(false)
}

I added `PUT /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id` and unit tests for it. I did not add a migration, which departs from your request. I could not run the tests in this session, so they are unverified.

**Why no migration:** the repo has no separate edit marker. `Comment.updatedAt` already exists in `schema.prisma` and is the mark. The spec's rule 4 agrees: no migration. Nothing in the repo says what a new flag should contain, so I did not invent one. If you want an explicit `isEdited` column, I can add it as a migration folder.

**Your five questions**

1. **Edit time limit:** the repo does not define one. I enforce none, as the spec says.
2. **Edited mark:** `Comment.updatedAt` (`app/src/prisma/schema.prisma`, line 29). The new service sets it on every edit, as `updateArticle` does (`article.service.ts`, around line 354). A migration for a separate flag has no source rule, so none was written.
3. **Error shape and status codes:** `app/src/main.ts` sends the `HttpException` message as the JSON body with the `errorCode` as the status. The repo is not consistent about the body. Some throws use `{ message }`, some `{ errors: {...} } `, some `{}`. I followed the sibling comment actions.
4. **Migrations:** `app/README.md` says to apply with `npx prisma migrate deploy`. Migration folders are named `<timestamp>_<name>/migration.sql`. `migration_lock.toml` is not edited by hand. None of this was needed here.
5. **Unit tests:** they live in `app/src/tests/services/` and match `jest.config.ts`'s `*.test.ts` pattern. Run them with `npm test`, which runs `nx test`. Mocks come from `src/tests/prisma-mock.ts`.

**Rules applied**

| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Auth required | Bearer or Token header; missing credentials return 401 | `article.controller.ts` (`auth.required`), `main.ts` |
| Author only | Lookup filters on comment id and author id. Non-author gets 404 | `article.service.ts`, `deleteComment` |
| Author-only conflict | `updateArticle` returns 403 for non-author. I followed `deleteComment`, which the spec names | `article.service.ts`, `updateArticle` vs `deleteComment` |
| Missing body | 422 with `{ errors: { body: ["can't be blank"] } }` | `article.service.ts`, `addComment` |
| Not found | 404 with `{}` | `article.service.ts`, `deleteComment` |
| Success response | 200 with `{ comment: {...} }`, same comment shape as create | `article.controller.ts` (POST comments), `addComment`. The spec does not name this shape; this is my assumption |
| Edit marker | `updatedAt` set to `new Date()` | `schema.prisma`, `updateArticle` |
| Edit time limit | None found | Not in repo; assumed none |
| Migrations | `npx prisma migrate deploy`; no migration added | `app/README.md`, `migrations/` |
| Unit tests | `*.test.ts` under `src/tests/`; `npm test` | `jest.config.ts`, `project.json`, `package.json` |

**My own choice, not in any rule source:** the lookup also requires the comment to belong to the article in the URL. A comment id from another article returns 404. `deleteComment` does not check this.

**Changed files** (all under `app/`):
- `src/app/routes/article/article.service.ts`: new `updateComment`.
- `src/app/routes/article/article.controller.ts`: the PUT route.
- `src/tests/services/article.service.test.ts`: three tests. Author edit succeeds, non-author gets 404 and no update, empty body gets 422.

The spec file in `specs/` is unchanged.
